event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: AVGO’s 2022 Form 10-K repeatedly links the COVID-19 pandemic to concrete and ongoing operational, supply-chain and workforce hazards.  The company discloses that the pandemic has already disrupted semiconductor sourcing, increased input costs, forced lengthened customer lead-times, triggered logistics delays and compelled a build-to-order production stance— all of which are direct, realized impacts, not merely hypothetical.  Forward-looking language stresses that these headwinds ‘may continue,’ could ‘recur,’ and remain subject to uncontrollable variables such as new variants and vaccine uptake, underscoring the persistence of risk.  Mitigating steps (employee safety measures) are acknowledged but portrayed as potentially inadequate.  Because the filing date (Dec-2022) is less than three years after the WHO declaration (Mar-2020), the Time Decay Principle allows high severity scores.  Overall, the pandemic is depicted as a recent, multifaceted risk with tangible operational consequences and only partial mitigations, meriting upper-tier risk scores across the extracted evidence.

evidence_list.snippet: Many of the following risks and uncertainties are, and may continue to be, exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Explicitly states that COVID-19 worsens multiple corporate risks.
Uses forward-looking language ('may continue'), signalling persistence.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: General statement of exacerbation and continuation; moderately severe but generic, so 4/10.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted normal business activity.

components.reason: Declares an actual, company-level disruption already occurred.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct acknowledgment of realized disruption, but no specifics or magnitude, yielding 4/10.

evidence_list.snippet: Further, any substantial disruption in the contract manufacturing services that we utilize, including TSMC’s supply of wafers to us, as a result of a natural disaster, climate change, water shortages, political unrest, military conflicts, geopolitical turmoil, trade tensions, government orders, medical epidemics, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, economic instability, equipment failure or other cause, could materially harm our business, customer relationships and results of operations.

components.reason: Links COVID-19 to potential disruption of critical wafer supply chain.
Uses strong materiality language ('could materially harm').
Forward-looking conditional rather than realized.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specifies supply-chain vulnerability and material harm, largely prospective, so 6/10.

evidence_list.snippet: For example, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, we have experienced some supply constraints and increases in prices, including with respect to wafers and substrates.

components.reason: States concrete past impact: supply constraints and higher costs.
Identifies specific inputs (wafers, substrates).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Realized cost and supply pressure on key materials makes this strong evidence (6/10).

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted normal business activity, which has impacted how we operate our business.

components.reason: Restates business disruption and direct operational impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct but still broad statement of operational impact; no detail, score 4/10.

evidence_list.snippet: We experienced some disruption to parts of our global semiconductor supply chain, including procuring necessary components and inputs, such as wafers and substrates, in a timely fashion, with suppliers increasing lead times or placing products on allocation.

components.reason: Details actual supply-chain disruption and delayed procurement.
Specifies lead-time extensions and allocation measures.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Provides concrete, realized operational effects—lead-time and allocations—earning 6/10.

evidence_list.snippet: As a result of these supply chain disruptions, we increased customer order lead times and placed some products on allocation.

components.reason: Shows internal response to pandemic pressures (longer lead times, allocations).
Indicates inability to meet demand, directly affecting customers.

evidence_list.snippet: We are also largely building semiconductor products to order and this has limited and may continue to limit our ability to fulfill orders and satisfy all of the demand for our products.

components.reason: Describes capacity limitation already in effect (build-to-order).
Highlights ongoing risk of unmet demand ('may continue').

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Evidence of constrained fulfilment with forward risk, moderate impact 4/10.

evidence_list.snippet: The pandemic resulted in authorities around the world implementing numerous unprecedented measures, such as travel restrictions quarantines, shelter-in-place order, and factory and office shutdowns, that impacted our workforce and operations, and those of our customers, CMs, suppliers and logistics providers.

components.reason: Links external governmental actions to multi-layered operational impact.
Specifies workforce effects and partner disruptions.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows broad ecosystem impact; no numeric magnitude, so 5/10.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, disruptions to commercial transportation infrastructure impacted delivery times for materials and components to our facilities, transfers of our products to our key suppliers and, in some cases, our ability to timely ship our products to customers.

components.reason: Identifies logistics bottlenecks affecting inbound and outbound shipping.
Specifies direct consequence: delayed customer shipments.

evidence_list.snippet: This resulted in significant logistical challenges and product delays, which could recur in the event of any future closures of, or periods of reduced operations at, our warehouse or the facilities of our suppliers and providers.

components.reason: Reports 'significant' delays already experienced.
Warns of recurrence risk, extending horizon.

evidence_list.snippet: In response to the pandemic, we have taken extensive measures to protect the health and safety of our employees and contractors at our facilities.

components.reason: Indicates mitigation efforts undertaken.

evidence_list.snippet: However, existing or new precautionary measures or modifications in our business practices and policies, may negatively impact our business or operations, especially if the spread of COVID-19 (including any variants) worsens significantly.

components.reason: Admits that mitigation steps themselves can harm operations.
Highlights variant-driven worsening scenario.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Moderate prospective risk tied to variant uncertainty; 3/10.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, any actions we take may not be sufficient to mitigate the risk of infection and could result in a significant number of COVID-19-related claims.

components.reason: Acknowledges limits of mitigation and potential legal liabilities.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Introduces litigation/health liability exposure; moderate severity 3/10.

evidence_list.snippet: If a significant number of our employees, or employees and third parties performing key functions, including our Chief Executive Officer and members of our Board of Directors, become ill, our business may be further adversely impacted.

components.reason: Describes potential critical-personnel illness impacting governance and operations.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specifies key-person risk; contingent but material, 3/10.

evidence_list.snippet: The degree to which the pandemic ultimately impacts our business and results of operations will depend on future developments beyond our control, including the extent of actions to contain the virus (including any variants), availability and efficacy of the vaccines or other treatments, public acceptance of the vaccines (including boosters), and to what extent normal economic and operating conditions resume.

components.reason: Highlights high uncertainty and dependency on external factors.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Notes uncertainty; lower immediacy and specificity, thus 2/10.
